title: Review of the CIPS consumer claim on fresh seed 7: X and E replicate (frozen 75-droplet twin vs a dividing prey population; all consumers gone within 100 t of prey removal), but consumers are short-lived bands (median track 400 t, 29% born by nucleation, 0 persistent tracks), so I and D are not supported
summary: labkit re-run of the claimed world (seed 7, 128^2, t=12000, --lineage-k 5): prey 83 persistent splits, generation 8; consumers 30 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.05; but 0 persistent tracks of either species. Consumer-free twin (pred_on 0, same seed and settings): 75 static prey, 1 persistent split, 1 moving track. Prey-removal fork at t=3000 (tcut): consumers 31 -> 0 and prey 39 -> 0 by t=3100, while the fed run keeps 31 -> 25 consumers. Per-species tracking rebuilt from the rendered channels (lifetimes.py): consumer tracks after t=500 live a median 400 t (p90 1000 t), and 184 of 637 begin by nucleation from the bath rather than by a split; the consumers are bands on prey edges (pack/sheet.png).

observations.S: pack/sheet.png t=0: prey and enzyme noise over the whole box; prey droplets with consumer bands by t=500
observations.X: pack vs twin (seed 7, same grid, duration, window): prey 83 vs 1 persistent splits, 109 vs 1 moving tracks, 39 vs 75 bodies at the end; consumers lower prey number and make the prey divide and move
observations.E: efork_s7.txt: prey removed at t=3000, consumers 31 -> 0 by t=3100 (fed run 31 -> 25); the enzyme is never made from prey

seeds_run.result: X and E reproduce; consumer I and D do not meet the gates (0 persistent tracks, median consumer track 400 t, 29% nucleation births)

controls_run.E: efork/ (tcut 3000, seed 7) against pack/ (fed, same seed): efork_s7.txt

verdicts.limitation: I and D are not supported: on my seed the consumers are bands lying on prey edges whose tracks last a median 400 t (p75 600, p90 1000) against ~100-200 t to form, 0 of 732 consumer tracks persist half the run, and 184 of 637 consumer tracks after t=500 start by nucleation from the enzyme bath, so many consumers have no parent; consumer 'splits' are the band being cut when its prey pinches. The prey also churn (median track 400 t, 0 persistent) once consumers cut them. Because I fails, the X and E I support are population-level effects of consumer condensates, not shown on the same long-lived individuals. One fresh seed; labkit counts, with lifetimes rebuilt from rendered frames (100 t apart).
